findings.highlight: inconcealable desperation
findings.evidenceJa: 覆しようのない絶望
findings.governingReading: despair that cannot be overturned
findings.explanation: Inconcealable concerns hiding emotion; the source says the despairing outcome cannot be reversed. Desperation also shifts 絶望 from absence of hope to urgent effort.

findings.highlight: even Caster herself without any difficulty
findings.evidenceJa: 逃げようとするキャスターすら、事も無げに始末した
findings.governingReading: effortlessly disposed even of Caster as she tried to escape
findings.explanation: The English omits that Caster was attempting to flee when the golden Servant finished her.

findings.highlight: At a distance with which we could start fighting if we wanted to face a “death” greater than Berserker.
findings.evidenceJa: その気になればすぐにでも斬り合いを始められる距離
findings.governingReading: At a distance close enough that a swordfight could begin the instant either side chose
findings.explanation: The English attaches the Berserker comparison to wanting to fight and produces a malformed spatial sentence, obscuring how immediately violence can begin.

findings.highlight: The chance of success of retreating from a guy like this is low.
findings.evidenceJa: あまりにも成功率が低すぎる
findings.governingReading: The chance of escaping is far, far too low.
findings.explanation: Low removes the emphatic excess expressed by both あまりにも and 低すぎる.

findings.highlight: For some reason, I know
findings.evidenceJa: 確証もなく思った
findings.governingReading: He thinks it without any firm evidence.
findings.explanation: The English reverses explicit lack of certainty into knowledge.

findings.highlight: It should be able to shelter you even against him
findings.evidenceJa: あいつなら、アレが相手でもおまえを匿ってくれる筈
findings.governingReading: Kotomine should shelter Saber even from that enemy.
findings.explanation: The English makes the church building the sheltering actor, erasing Shirou’s reliance on Kotomine as a person.

findings.highlight: I shall let you live until the Holy Grail appears.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を呼ぶまでは生かしておいてやろう
findings.governingReading: He will keep Shirou alive until the Grail is summoned.
findings.explanation: Appears removes the deliberate ritual act of calling forth the Grail.

findings.highlight: I will kill you if you annoy me.
findings.evidenceJa: それ以上さえずるのなら殺すぞ
findings.governingReading: If Shirou chirps or prattles any further, he will be killed.
findings.explanation: Annoy me replaces a concrete condition—continuing to speak—with the enemy’s subjective irritation.

findings.highlight: he will do so without hesitation
findings.evidenceJa: なんの苦労もかけずに実行する
findings.governingReading: he will carry out the killing without the slightest effort or trouble
findings.explanation: Without hesitation changes ease of execution into decisiveness.

findings.highlight: after being told that
findings.evidenceJa: そんな事実を見せつけられて
findings.governingReading: after having that fact forcibly demonstrated before him
findings.explanation: Told reduces bodily proof of overwhelming power to verbal information.

findings.highlight: you are not willing to come to me
findings.evidenceJa: 我に下る気はない
findings.governingReading: you still have no intention of submitting to me
findings.explanation: Come to me replaces political and personal submission with physical approach.

findings.highlight: I do not want to live with you.
findings.evidenceJa: まかり間違ってもありえません
findings.governingReading: Living with him is absolutely impossible under any conceivable circumstances.
findings.explanation: Do not want reduces Saber’s categorical impossibility to personal preference.

findings.highlight: drives magical energy into her sword
findings.evidenceJa: 有り余る魔力を剣に載せ
findings.governingReading: loads her sword with her overflowing surplus of magical power
findings.explanation: The English removes the excessive abundance that powers Saber’s lightning-like barrage.

findings.highlight: The man hasn’t even drawn his weapon yet.
findings.evidenceJa: 男は帯剣していない
findings.governingReading: The man is not carrying or wearing a sword.
findings.explanation: Not drawn implies a present sheathed weapon; the source says he is not bearing a sword at all.

findings.highlight: And on top of that, Saber’s sword is invisible.
findings.evidenceJa: 加えて、セイバーの剣は不可視だ
findings.governingReading: Japanese page51 continues the sword analysis; its English counterpart should occupy the same label.
findings.explanation: The comparator has no page51 and instead labels this passage as the first of two page53 occurrences, breaking label-level alignment.

findings.highlight: keeps hitting the man’s armor
findings.evidenceJa: 面白いように、男の鎧に直撃する
findings.governingReading: strikes the man’s armor with almost absurd or gratifying ease
findings.explanation: The English omits the narrator’s evaluation of how readily every invisible blow lands.

findings.highlight: one-sided elimination
findings.evidenceJa: 一方的な殲滅戦
findings.governingReading: a one-sided war of annihilation
findings.explanation: Elimination is an awkward result noun and removes the scale and combat framing of 戦.

findings.highlight: You certainly do have a large supply of magical energy.
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず底なしの魔力
findings.governingReading: Saber’s magical power remains as bottomless as ever.
findings.explanation: Large supply weakens the enemy’s claim from effectively unfathomable reserves to ordinary abundance.

findings.highlight: My armor does not give out often
findings.evidenceJa: 我の鎧が軋みをあげるなど、そうあり得る事ではない
findings.governingReading: It is exceedingly rare for his armor even to creak under strain.
findings.explanation: Giving out changes the armor’s first audible strain into outright failure and alters the threshold of Saber’s achievement.

findings.highlight: Saber distances herself
findings.evidenceJa: 二度間合いを離し
findings.governingReading: Saber disengages and opens the interval for a second time.
findings.explanation: The English removes that this is Saber’s second deliberate separation, weakening the developing tactical pattern.

findings.highlight: his armor is at its limit
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツの鎧も限界が近い
findings.governingReading: his armor is nearing its limit
findings.explanation: The English promotes proximity to the limit into arrival at it.

findings.highlight: Saber’s body stops.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの体がズレる
findings.governingReading: Saber’s body slips or is displaced off line.
findings.explanation: Stops replaces lateral displacement under the unexpected weapon exchange with cessation of movement.

findings.highlight: Saber retreats, covered in ice.
findings.evidenceJa: 氷に覆われながらも咄嗟に後退する
findings.governingReading: Even while ice covers her, Saber retreats instantly on reflex.
findings.explanation: The English omits the concessive resistance and split-second response.

findings.highlight: a sickle-like weapon
findings.evidenceJa: 死神の鎌めいた凶器
findings.governingReading: a lethal weapon resembling the Grim Reaper’s scythe
findings.explanation: Sickle-like removes the death-personification image and weakens 凶器 into a neutral weapon.

findings.highlight: As if cutting away her bone
findings.evidenceJa: 骨そのものを抜き取るかのように
findings.governingReading: as though pulling the bone itself out of the targeted place
findings.explanation: Cutting changes an extraction simile into severing and makes the imagined bodily mechanism more literal.

findings.highlight: drawing magical energy into her arm
findings.evidenceJa: 麻痺した片腕に魔力を通しながら
findings.governingReading: channeling magical power through her one paralyzed arm
findings.explanation: The English omits both paralysis and that only one arm is affected.

findings.highlight: Many handles
findings.evidenceJa: 無数の柄
findings.governingReading: countless weapon hilts
findings.explanation: Many reduces the explicitly innumerable scale that motivates Saber’s impossible-Noble-Phantasm reaction.

findings.highlight: all the divine mysteries from every legend
findings.evidenceJa: ありとあらゆる伝承に潜む神秘の全て
findings.governingReading: every mystery hidden within traditions of every age and place
findings.explanation: Divine adds godhood to 神秘 and removes the sense that these mysteries lie concealed within the traditions.

findings.highlight: if it was a fake
findings.evidenceJa: あの宝具が全て偽物であったのなら
findings.governingReading: if all of those Noble Phantasms were counterfeits
findings.explanation: The English changes the entire arsenal being false into one unspecified object being fake.

findings.highlight: the model of weapon
findings.evidenceJa: 原型の、武器
findings.governingReading: prototype weapons
findings.explanation: Model of weapon is malformed and can imply a representation; Shirou realizes “original” may mean archetypal prototypes.

findings.highlight: only those that originate in that land
findings.evidenceJa: その土地に帰順した物だけ
findings.governingReading: only traditions that submitted or became assimilated to that land
findings.explanation: Originate reverses the relation: the source describes traditions adapted to a land, not necessarily born there.

findings.highlight: They were valued because they were splendid swords
findings.evidenceJa: 名剣であるが故に重宝され活躍し
findings.governingReading: Because they were celebrated blades, they were prized and saw active use.
findings.explanation: The English omits the weapons’ subsequent deeds, the step by which scattered treasury objects become later Noble Phantasms.

findings.highlight: One said to rule over ancient Mesopotamia.
findings.evidenceJa: 古代メソポタミアに君臨したという魔人
findings.governingReading: the supernatural or demonic figure said to have reigned in ancient Mesopotamia
findings.explanation: The English omits 魔人, removing a key characterization immediately before the half-divine king’s identification.

findings.highlight: his many Noble Phantasms
findings.evidenceJa: 有り余る宝具
findings.governingReading: his superabundant, inexhaustible supply of Noble Phantasms
findings.explanation: Many removes the sense of surplus abundance established by the bottomless treasury.

findings.highlight: defeat his enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 敵を粉砕する
findings.governingReading: pulverize or crush the enemy
findings.explanation: Defeat neutralizes the violent totality of Gilgamesh’s intended finishing action.

findings.highlight: The pain is telling me I will break if I move any further.
findings.evidenceJa: 体中にはしった罅が、これ以上動けば砕けてしまう
findings.governingReading: The cracks running throughout his body warn that they will shatter if he moves farther.
findings.explanation: The English replaces concrete cracks and their impending propagation with a generalized personified pain.

findings.highlight: A holy sword
findings.evidenceJa: 音に聞こえし聖剣
findings.governingReading: the famed holy sword known by reputation
findings.explanation: The English omits Gilgamesh’s acknowledgment of Excalibur’s renown.

findings.highlight: try to defend yourself against my sword
findings.evidenceJa: 我が剣、見事受けきってみるがいい
findings.governingReading: Try to withstand my sword completely and magnificently.
findings.explanation: Defend yourself generalizes Saber’s challenge to receive the full attack without failing.

findings.highlight: battle of the two rumblings
findings.evidenceJa: 拮抗した両者の奔流
findings.governingReading: the two opposing torrents locked in equilibrium
findings.explanation: Rumblings replaces flows of power and the English phrase is malformed, obscuring the apparent stalemate before reversal.
